p:AFG:
DA AFGHANISTAN BANK
Afghanistan
Da Afghanistan Bank is Afghanistan's central bank and issues the afghani. It scores 33 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, its weak point being corruption in the country, while the independence written into its law scores 0.87 of 1, where 1 means the bank holds the power. In May 2011 Afghanistan's High Office of Oversight and Anticorruption reported that the central bank had monitored Kabul Bank poorly; Kabul Bank had 925 million dollars in loans outstanding, many of them undocumented and given to powerful figures, before the central bank took it over in 2010. After the Taliban took power, the United States froze nearly 9.5 billion dollars of the bank's assets on 17 August 2021, much of it held at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, and stopped shipments of cash. On 11 February 2022 President Joe Biden signed an order splitting 7 billion dollars of the frozen money in two: 3.5 billion for relief in Afghanistan and 3.5 billion kept in the United States for lawsuits by US victims of terrorism. The bank holds 21.9 tonnes of gold, and its 2018 accounts were audited by Ernst & Young Ford Rhodes Sidat Hyder. A news report of 6 January 2020 said the bank had awarded the Polish Security Printing Works a contract for new 10, 20, 50 and 100 afghani notes, and on 1 February 2021 the Polish embassy in New Delhi announced that the works had delivered 380 million printed banknotes; no contract value is given and nothing says the arrangement continues.

p:AGO:
NATIONAL BANK OF ANGOLA
Angola
The National Bank of Angola issues the kwanza (AOA). Angola scores 41 of 100 on exposure to influence, where 0 means shielded and 100 means fully exposed; its weakest side is secrecy about who owns money and corruption (index score 32 of 100). Government pressure was reported in 29 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, nearly all pressing the bank to cut rates or ease, with 8 threats to replace leaders. On 14 August 2020 the Supreme Court convicted former governor Valter Filipe (eight years), BNA manager Samalia (five years), José Filomeno dos Santos (five years) and businessman Sebastião (six years) of embezzlement, fraud and influence peddling over an attempted transfer of $500 million to a London account, which a British bank blocked. The Constitutional Court is also named in the case. Goznak, the Russian state printer, printed the 5,000-kwanza note. KPMG audits the bank's accounts, and signed off on the 2021 accounts with one reservation and seven emphases, against three reservations and six emphases the year before. The London firm Gemcorp Capital held 56 percent of the bank's external assets at the end of 2023, 601,697 million kwanzas or about 725 million US dollars. For the 2019 and 2020 accounts Gemcorp did not say what it had invested the central bank's money in, so the bank had to carry the holding at nil, and it then renewed the investment for a further six years. Both facts come from the newspaper Expansao reading the bank's accounts rather than from the accounts themselves: the bank's own website publishes no documents a reader can open.

p:AIA:
EASTERN CARIBBEAN CENTRAL BANK
Anguilla
Anguilla has no central bank of its own: it uses the EC dollar, issued by the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, the monetary authority for eight places, Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, and St Vincent and the Grenadines. The currency has been fixed at EC$2.70 to one US dollar since July 1976, when the peg moved from sterling, backed by a legal requirement to hold reserves of at least 60 per cent of currency in circulation. One case is recorded. The Official Stanford Investors Committee sued the bank in Dallas in 2013 after it seized the Stanford-owned Bank of Antigua, alleging it fraudulently misappropriated assets belonging to Stanford's victims and creditors. On 17 August 2018 a US federal judge dismissed the claims in full because the bank and Antigua are immune under US foreign sovereign immunity law, and did not rule on whether the allegations were true. For Anguilla the arrangement scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. In a letter dated 17 February 2025 to Antigua and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne, who chairs the ECCU Monetary Council, St Vincent and the Grenadines Prime Minister Ralph Gonsalves objected to the EC$22 million spent on an official residence for Governor Timothy Antoine, calling the spending outrageous and the roughly 10,000 square foot house a mansion of veritable palace proportions. Gonsalves wrote that the governor may wish to consider whether his continued occupancy of the office is tenable, and that the spending invites disciplinary action; he proposed that the Monetary Council, which is made up of the member states' finance ministers, sell the residence to the government of St Kitts and Nevis, and said he had supported Antoine's appointment but wanted suitable and comfortable accommodation for him instead. On 5 March 2025 Gonsalves told NBC Radio he would neither confirm nor deny sending the letter. The World Bank has a hand in running the reserves: the bank's 2020/2021 annual report says it continued its engagement with the World Bank's Reserves Advisory Management Partnership (RAMP), and that a second engagement was judged appropriate to go on building up its newly formed Risk and Analytics Unit, the unit that reports on the reserves portfolio. The same report says the investment guidelines for the bank's external managers were reviewed and updated, and that the foreign reserve portfolio had grown to about EC$4.6 billion. The engagement is not repeated in the later annual report for 2024/2025 or in the audited accounts to 31 March 2025, so it stands as a 2020/2021 fact. De La Rue supplies the polymer the notes are made on and, by one report on the updated banknote family announced on 9 July 2026, prints them; PricewaterhouseCoopers Eastern Caribbean audits the accounts.

Eastern Caribbean Currency Union (monetary union)

The ECCB is the monetary authority for Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
The ECCB agreement was signed on 5 July 1983 and the Bank was commissioned on 1 October 1983.
The EC dollar has been fixed at EC$2.70 = US$1.00 since July 1976, when the peg moved from sterling to the US dollar.
Section 24(2) of the ECCB Agreement Act requires an external reserve of not less than 60% of currency in circulation and other demand liabilities.
The IMF AREAER 2023 classification lists the ECCU members as a currency board.

BANK OF ALBANIA
Albania
The Bank of Albania is Albania's central bank and issues the lek, kept close to the euro without any formal promise to do so; it scores 25 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. In July 2014 one of its employees was found to have stolen 713 million lek, nearly seven million US dollars, from the reserves. On 5 September 2014 prosecutors arrested governor Fullani and the bank's senior auditor and charged them with abuse of office over alleged mismanagement linked to that theft; the board dismissed Fullani, and the charges remain unproven, with no verdict reported. In September 2014 parliament voted 72 to 6 to dismiss Ardian Fullani, who had been appointed in 2004 and was serving a second seven-year term, after the bank's executive board argued that he posed a grave threat to the bank's interests. He was jailed earlier that month and later moved to house arrest, and seventeen other central bank employees were arrested; Fullani denied wrongdoing and was not accused of personally profiting, and Elisabeta Gjoni served as acting governor. No government pressure was reported in 37 quarters to 2018. The bank signed a swap line with China for 2 billion yuan on 3 April 2018, letting the two central banks lend each other their currencies; a borrowing line with the European Central Bank expired on 15 January 2024. Gent Sejko has been Governor and Chairman of the Supervisory Council since 5 February 2015 and was re-elected for a second term on 24 February 2022; immediately before that appointment he was Deputy General Manager of Societe Generale Albania, a commercial bank, and earlier he held senior posts at the National Commercial Bank, the American Bank of Albania and Raiffeisen Bank.

CENTRAL BANK OF THE UAE
United Arab Emirates
The Central Bank of the United Arab Emirates issues the dirham and holds it at a fixed rate against the US dollar, an arrangement called a peg. It scores 29 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. On Saturday 29 August 2026 the bank said it had ordered a special and urgent examination of the UAE branches of Banque Misr, an Egyptian lender with five branches in the country, after the United States raised money-laundering concerns; the US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network had proposed a rule that would revoke Banque Misr UAE's correspondent banking access to US financial institutions. The bank said the examination includes a forensic, in-depth lookback over the period covered by the US statement and focuses on transactions of the companies named in it, that it was studying options for the bank's status if the US special measure is formally imposed, and that it expects banks it licenses to avoid reputational risks to the financial system and to respect other countries' laws. Nothing has been proven against Banque Misr; these are concerns raised by the US authorities and an examination ordered by the UAE central bank. The same report noted that in June 2026 a foreign bank branch in the UAE, not named, was fined 20 million dirhams, about 5.44 million US dollars, for anti-money-laundering failures. No government pressure was reported in the 37 quarters surveyed between 2010 and 2018. Its law gives it middling independence, 0.685 of 1. It is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. Its notes are printed by Oumolat Security Printing, which the Emirates Investment Authority started and owned before it was transferred to the central bank; a new 100 dirham polymer note printed by Oumolat was reported on 31 March 2025. Abdulhamid Saeed, made governor by federal decree on 2 April 2020, had been group chief executive of First Abu Dhabi Bank.

p:ARG:
CENTRAL BANK OF THE ARGENTINE REPUBLIC
Argentina
Argentina's money is the peso, issued by the Central Bank of the Argentine Republic, which scores 39 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Luis Caputo, its president from June 2018 until he resigned on 25 September 2018, had headed bond and equity trading at JP Morgan Argentina in the 1990s and presided over Deutsche Bank in Argentina from 2003 to 2008. In January 2010 the government called on governor Martin Redrado to resign after he refused to back a decree releasing 6.6 billion dollars of reserves, then fired him; he resigned that month, the reserves stayed frozen and a court held that the full Congress had to approve their use. Fifteen people, among them Cristina Fernandez de Kirchner and economy minister Axel Kicillof, were tried over the bank's 2015 dollar-futures sales, and the case against all of them was dismissed on 13 April 2021. In May 2023, an election year, the bank advanced a further 140 billion pesos to the Treasury, using 99.2 per cent of the limit agreed with the International Monetary Fund. It is examining at least 900 million dollars bought at the official rate in 2022 and 2023 that allegedly reached the parallel market; the firms deny it and nothing is proven. Its notes have moved around: the state mint, Casa de Moneda, printed 1,000- and 2,000-peso notes under contracts of November 2021, September 2022 and February 2023, the bank partly cancelled them and the mint stopped printing at 10pm on 28 October 2024. Production of the 2,000-peso note had gone to Spain's Fábrica Nacional de Moneda y Timbre, and 20,000-peso notes were imported from China. In July 2026 President Javier Milei announced a bill to bar the bank from funding the state.

CENTRAL BANK OF ARMENIA
Armenia
Armenia uses the dram, issued by the Central Bank of Armenia, which scores 20 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. The dram is held on a pre-announced crawling peg against the US dollar, meaning the rate is moved in small announced steps. No case at the bank is recorded, and no government pressure was reported in the 37 quarters surveyed between 2010 and 2018. The bank has rejoined the World Bank Treasury's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership, having been a member from 2006 to 2014; what it gets is advice, onsite expertise and staff training rather than management of its assets. It has one swap line with China, an arrangement for two central banks to lend each other currency, for 77 billion drams and one billion yuan, dated March 2015, though whether it is still in force is not known. A bank representative says Giesecke+Devrient won the printing of its third banknote series after an evaluation of all offers. KPMG Armenia LLC audits the accounts.

p:ATG:
EASTERN CARIBBEAN CENTRAL BANK
Antigua & Barbuda
Antigua and Barbuda uses the East Caribbean dollar, issued by the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, which sets monetary policy for eight members, among them Anguilla, Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat and Saint Lucia. The currency has been fixed at 2.70 East Caribbean dollars to one US dollar since July 1976, and the law requires an external reserve worth at least 60 per cent of the currency in circulation and other demand liabilities. Its laws score 0.549 of 1 on one measure of independence and 0.642 on another, where 1 means the bank rather than the government holds the power; the rules on lending to government score 0.08 on the first. Government pressure was reported in none of the 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018. In a letter dated 17 February 2025 to Antigua and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne, who chairs the ECCU Monetary Council, St Vincent and the Grenadines Prime Minister Ralph Gonsalves objected to the EC$22 million spent on an official residence for Governor Timothy Antoine, calling the spending outrageous and the roughly 10,000 square foot house a mansion of veritable palace proportions. Gonsalves wrote that the governor may wish to consider whether his continued occupancy of the office is tenable, and that the spending invites disciplinary action; he proposed that the Monetary Council, made up of the member states' finance ministers, sell the residence to the government of St Kitts and Nevis, and said he had supported Antoine's appointment but wanted suitable and comfortable accommodation for him instead. On 5 March 2025 Gonsalves told NBC Radio he would neither confirm nor deny sending the letter. In one case the Official Stanford Investors Committee sued the bank in Dallas in 2013, alleging it fraudulently misappropriated assets after it seized the Stanford-owned Bank of Antigua; on 17 August 2018 a US federal judge dismissed the claims in full because the bank and Antigua are immune under US foreign sovereign immunity law, and the court did not rule on whether the allegations were true. The exposure score is 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence; the highest part is corruption and secrecy around it, at 53. De La Rue prints the notes and PricewaterhouseCoopers Eastern Caribbean audits the accounts. The World Bank has a hand in running the reserves: the bank's 2020/2021 annual report says it continued its engagement with the World Bank's Reserves Advisory Management Partnership (RAMP), and that a second engagement was judged appropriate to go on building up its newly formed Risk and Analytics Unit, the unit that reports on the reserves portfolio. The same report says the investment guidelines for the bank's external managers were reviewed and updated, and that the foreign reserve portfolio had grown to about EC$4.6 billion. The engagement is not repeated in the later annual report for 2024/2025 or in the audited accounts to 31 March 2025, so it stands as a 2020/2021 fact.

2025-02-17 · public pressure. In a letter dated 17 February 2025 to Antigua and Barbuda Prime Minister Gaston Browne, who chairs the ECCU Monetary Council, St Vincent and the Grenadines Prime Minister Ralph Gonsalves objected to the EC$22 million spent on an official residence for Eastern Caribbean Central Bank Governor Timothy Antoine, calling the spending outrageous and the roughly 10,000 square foot house a mansion of veritable palace proportions. Gonsalves wrote that the governor may wish to consider whether his continued occupancy of the office is tenable, and that the spending invites disciplinary action. He proposed that the Monetary Council sell the residence to the government of St Kitts and Nevis, and said he had supported Antoine's appointment but wanted suitable and comfortable accommodation for him instead. On 5 March 2025 Gonsalves told NBC Radio he would neither confirm nor deny sending the letter. The Monetary Council is made up of the member states' finance ministers, so this is pressure from heads of government on the union's own central bank. Eastern Caribbean Currency Union (monetary union)

The ECCB is the monetary authority for Anguilla, Antigua and Barbuda, Dominica, Grenada, Montserrat, St Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
The ECCB agreement was signed on 5 July 1983 and the Bank was commissioned on 1 October 1983.

Section 24(2) of the ECCB Agreement Act requires an external reserve of not less than 60% of currency in circulation and other demand liabilities.
The IMF AREAER 2023 classification lists the ECCU members as a currency board.

RESERVE BANK OF AUSTRALIA
Australia
The Reserve Bank of Australia issues the Australian dollar, which floats freely. It scores 24 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and no government pressure was reported from 2010 to 2018. On 14 July 2023 the government announced that governor Philip Lowe would not be reappointed when his term ended that September, breaking the custom by which the two previous governors were each given a second term. Lowe had been widely criticised after telling the public rates were unlikely to rise before 2024 and then raising the cash rate from 0.1 to 4.1 percent; that criticism led the treasurer to commission an independent review of the bank, whose recommendations to change how it is run and how policy is made the government accepted in full. Its one case came out of its own banknote businesses: in October 2011 the subsidiaries Securency and Note Printing Australia pleaded guilty to conspiring to bribe foreign officials to win banknote work from the note-issuing authorities of Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and Nepal, paying proceeds-of-crime penalties of 19.8 million and 1.86 million Australian dollars and fines of 480,000 and 450,000. Securency's former chief financial officer got a suspended six-month sentence for false accounting in 2012, the agent Radius Christanto a suspended two-year sentence in 2013. Three governors went into private finance on leaving: Ian Macfarlane to the ANZ board in 2007, Glenn Stevens to Macquarie Group in 2017 and Philip Lowe to Barrenjoey in 2024. Almost all its gold, 80 tonnes as at 30 June 2026, sits at the Bank of England, which holds it as bailee: storage, not management, with title staying with the Reserve Bank.

2023-07-14 · public pressure. On 14 July 2023 Treasurer Jim Chalmers and Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that Reserve Bank of Australia governor Philip Lowe would not be reappointed and would leave when his seven-year term ended on 17 September, after 43 years at the bank. Deputy governor Michele Bullock was appointed in his place. Lowe had been heavily criticised, particularly in the media, after telling the public that rates were unlikely to rise before 2024 and then raising the cash rate from 0.1 to 4.1 percent. That criticism led Chalmers to commission an independent review of the central bank, which recommended sweeping changes to how it is run and how policy is made, and which the government accepted in full. The previous two governors had each been reappointed to a further term as a matter of custom; asked why Lowe was not, Chalmers said extending a governor's tenure was "the exception rather than the rule" and that Bullock was best placed to implement the review. Australia appoints first female head for central bank (Reuters, via Inquirer Business)

OESTERREICHISCHE NATIONALBANK
Austria
Austria uses the euro: the European Central Bank sets its interest rates, for the 21 euro countries together, with the Oesterreichische Nationalbank taking part; the ECB is one of 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements. The national bank owns its banknote printer, OeBS, which cooperates with two other central-bank-owned printers. Managers of OeBS paid kickbacks to win orders, overcharging Azerbaijan's central bank by 20 percent and Syria's by 14 percent, about 14 million euros. Seven were convicted in October 2014; after a retrial, a Vienna court in February 2018 gave Wolf and Miller 18-month suspended sentences and Meyer 21 months suspended, and acquitted former deputy governor Duchatczek. In January 2018 the European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, ruled that ECB president Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a club of central bankers and private bankers, was maladministration; the ECB declined to drop it. In 2015 a speech by board member Coeure on front-loading asset purchases reached a private London audience the evening before publication; the ECB called this an internal procedure error. BDO Assurance, elected on 23 March 2023, audited the bank's 2025 accounts. The government that took office in 2017, the People's Party with the Freedom Party, planned to take banking supervision away from the bank. In April 2019 the bank said publicly that this threatened its financial independence: the draft law would have paid 95 percent of its profits to the federal government instead of the 90 percent then in force, which it said cuts its ability to build reserves, and it expected supervision costs to rise under more complicated structures that included three new sections inside the Finance Ministry. The Finance Ministry answered that it was following European best practice, that a payout rate of 95 percent or more existed in countries including the Netherlands, and that the change was structural and aimed at efficiency rather than personal. The reform did not take effect and the bank still supervises banks. Austria scores 24 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. Its gold is kept in two places inside the country: the bank says that of Austria's total gold reserves of 280 tons, 140 tons are stored in Austria, 90 tons in its own vaults, and 50 tons sit in the vaults of one of its subsidiaries, Münze Österreich AG, the Austrian Mint; the 280 tons correspond to some 22,400 gold bars. Seven career moves are recorded between the bank or the ECB and private finance: Ewald Nowotny went from chief executive of BAWAG P.S.K. to governor of the Oesterreichische Nationalbank from 2008; Otmar Issing, the ECB's former chief economist, accepted an offer in October 2006 to act as an international adviser to Goldman Sachs; Jörg Asmussen sat on the ECB Executive Board from 2012 to 2013 and moved in 2016 to the investment bank Lazard; José Manuel González-Páramo served on the ECB Executive Board from 2004 to 2012 and was appointed an Executive Board member of BBVA in June 2013; Lorenzo Bini Smaghi sat on the ECB Executive Board from June 2005 to December 2011 and has chaired the board of Société Générale since 2015; Luis de Guindos was Chief Executive Officer Iberia at Lehman Brothers and Chief Executive Officer at Nomura Securities from 2006 to 2008 and has been ECB Vice-President from 2018; and Peter Praet was Chief Economist of Générale de Banque and Fortis Bank from 1988 to 1999 before joining the ECB Executive Board in 2011.

2019-04-15 · attempted law change. The coalition of Sebastian Kurz's People's Party and the Freedom Party announced plans in 2018 to reform banking supervision in Austria, which is split between the Financial Market Authority and the Oesterreichische Nationalbank, by stripping the central bank of its supervisory role. In April 2019 the OeNB publicly accused the government of seeking to undermine its financial independence. It objected to two things. The first was cost: it said supervision costs in Austria would rise under the new and more complicated structures, in particular because three new sections would be created inside the Finance Ministry. The second was the method of paying for that. The draft law provided for 95 percent of the central bank's profits to be paid to the federal government instead of the 90 percent then in force, which the bank said reduces its ability to build reserves and should therefore be seen as an encroachment on its financial independence. In its formal comments on the draft law, reported in May 2019, the OeNB said the independence of both the central bank and the banking watchdog was damaged by the plans. The Finance Ministry answered that it was following European best practice and what is common in many European countries, that a payout rate of 95 percent or more existed in countries including the Netherlands, and that the decision was structural and aimed at efficiency rather than personal. The reform did not take effect: the OeNB still carries out banking supervision and reported reorganising that function itself in 2025. Austrian central bank says government threatens its financial independence (Reuters)

CENTRAL BANK OF THE REPUBLIC OF AZERBAIJAN
Azerbaijan
The Central Bank of the Republic of Azerbaijan issues the national currency, coded AZN, held at a de facto fixed rate against the US dollar. It scores 31 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, with corruption and secrecy around it at 62. On 12 April 2022 parliament approved President Ilham Aliyev's proposal to replace governor Elman Rustamov, in post since 1995, with Taleh Kazimov, head of Pasha Bank; Rustamov became adviser to the prime minister, and no official reason and no statement from him were reported. One career move is documented, and it is Kazimov's: at the private PASHA Bank, set up in 2007, he rose from risk manager to chief executive officer and then chairman, with no years given for those posts, and he then became governor of the central bank on the parliamentary vote reported on 18 April 2022. Two cases are documented. A Vienna court found that the Austrian banknote printer OeBS had overcharged the bank by 20 per cent on banknote contracts and that the kickback went back to local decision makers; OeBS managers were convicted in 2014 and again on retrial in 2018, and no Azerbaijani official was named or tried. Austrian prosecutors also told a court that former OeBS employees had paid bribes to officials at Syrian and Azerbaijani banks for printing contracts, which stands as a prosecution allegation. In September 2009 a Baku court sentenced six former officers of the bank to between a two-year suspended sentence and eight years for abuse of power and embezzling 1.4 million AZN between 2003 and 2008. KPMG Audit Azerbaijan LLC audits the accounts, and the bank holds no gold.

BANK OF THE REPUBLIC OF BURUNDI
Burundi
The Bank of the Republic of Burundi is the central bank of Burundi, which uses the Burundian franc. One case is recorded. In October 2023 the Ministry of Justice said that the dismissed governor, Dieudonné Murengerantwari, was being prosecuted for passive corruption (taking bribes), money laundering, misappropriation of public property and undermining the national economy. The prosecutor called this description of the facts provisional, and the governor was being questioned at the time of the report. He is charged, and nothing is reported as proven. The bank scores 34 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and its weakest side is corruption in the country. President Evariste Ndayishimiye fired the governor, Dieudonne Murengerantwari, on Sunday 8 October 2023, thirteen months into a five-year term. The presidency gave no reasons; bank employees told Yaga Burundi the removal was linked to misappropriation of foreign currency. Edouard Normand Bigendako, a board member, replaced him and inherited the same shortage of foreign exchange. Murengerantwari was then held by the National Intelligence Service and charged with undermining the proper functioning of the national economy, passive corruption, money laundering and misappropriation of public assets, charges the justice ministry called provisional and which he had not answered. Under his thirteen months the bank had loosened exchange policy, lifting restrictions on instant transfers received from abroad and suspending a 2016 decision that barred diplomatic missions and international organisations from holding foreign currency accounts outside commercial banks. NATIONAL BANK OF BELGIUM
Belgium
Belgium uses the euro, and the European Central Bank sets monetary policy for all 21 countries that use it; the National Bank of Belgium is the country's own central bank. Its 400,000 shares are split evenly: 200,000 registered shares are held by the Belgian State, fixed by law since 1948 and not transferable, and the other 200,000 trade on the Euronext Brussels stock exchange. Belgium scores 28 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Two findings stand against the European Central Bank. The European Ombudsman, the European Union's complaints office, found maladministration and in January 2018 recommended that its president, Mario Draghi, suspend his membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers; the bank declined and Draghi did not suspend it. On 18 May 2015 board member Benoît Cœuré told a private evening event in London that the bank would front-load its asset purchases, and the speech was published only the next morning, which the bank put down to an internal procedure error; Draghi said no market-sensitive information was revealed. Seven career moves between the bank and private finance are recorded, among them Tom Dechaene, who came from Deutsche Bank and the London merchant bank Morgan Grenfell and was made a director by a royal decree of 13 December 2014; those are job changes, not accusations. Most of the bank's 227,402.4 kilograms of gold is stored at the Bank of England, a much smaller portion at the Bank for International Settlements and the Bank of Canada, and a very limited quantity in the bank's own premises — storage, not management of the holding.

p:BEN:
CENTRAL BANK OF WEST AFRICAN STATES (BCEAO)
Benin
Benin does not have its own central bank. Its money is the West African CFA franc, issued by the Central Bank of West African States, known by its French initials BCEAO, which sets monetary policy for eight member countries. The franc is pegged, meaning held at a fixed rate, at one euro to 655.957 CFA francs, and France guarantees, without condition or limit, to advance euros if the BCEAO's reserves run out. A cooperation agreement signed in Abidjan on 21 December 2019 replaced the 1973 one and ended the requirement that the BCEAO keep at least half its reserves at the French Treasury, and France withdrew its representatives from the BCEAO board, its Monetary Policy Committee and the banking commission, though one independent committee member is still appointed in consultation with the French government. Benin scores 40 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, mainly from money-laundering risk in its banks and corruption in the country. One case is documented at the central bank: a summit of regional heads of state accepted governor Dacoury-Tabley's resignation in January 2011, after he was criticised for ignoring a 23 December decision by the union's finance ministers giving Alassane Ouattara power over the institution, and the account says the BCEAO paid out 60 to 100 billion CFA francs to the Gbagbo regime after that date. The bank's own statement said the resignation resulted from pressure from the region's leaders, and Dacoury-Tabley said afterwards that he agreed to hand it in because that is what was asked of him. Senegal's President Abdoulaye Wade asked for an audit and alleged the former governor moved 500 billion CFA francs, or by another figure 300 billion, to Gbagbo after being dismissed; no audit result is reported, so that is unproven. The accounts are audited by firms appointed in pairs, one doing the work and one standing in: Deloitte Benin with Mazars Benin for Benin, and Deloitte Cote d'Ivoire with Mazars Senegal for the BCEAO itself. Its money is printed in France. The French foreign ministry's own page on the Franc Zone says the African central banks place the orders for notes and coins under a contract with a manufacturer, in this case the Banque de France, and that CFA franc notes and coins have been made at its works at Chamalieres since 1945; the heads of state and government of the Franc Zone may decide together to change where they are printed. The Banque de France's own director general of banknote manufacturing has called the BCEAO its largest export customer. The BCEAO's published accounts do not name the maker. Its gold is mostly not in Africa. Note 6 of the BCEAO's own financial statements for 2024 lists three places: the bank's head office, the Banque de France and the Bank for International Settlements. On deposit at the Banque de France are 1,054,479.65 ounces, valued at 1,756,111 million CFA francs, out of a stock of about 1.52 million ounces worth 2,531,800 million, which is about 70 per cent; press reporting places it in the Banque de France's underground vault in the first arrondissement of Paris. The Bank for International Settlements holds close to 106,000 ounces, and only about 120,000 ounces, under 8 per cent, sit physically at the head office in Dakar. In the 2018 statements the Paris deposit was 85 per cent of holdings; the share has fallen because the rest of the stock grew, not because gold left Paris. Answering Senator Pierre Laurent on 20 October 2022, the French economy ministry said the rules for the deposit are set by a specific convention covering the services the Banque de France provides to the BCEAO, and that the gold, like the union's foreign exchange reserves, is pooled at the BCEAO rather than apportioned by country. The concentration is contested: pan-Africanist currents and some economists read it as a continuing post-colonial dependence and ask whether the gold will be repatriated as the member states' operating account deposits at the French Treasury were. Part of the reserves is run by outside institutions. The BCEAO's own audited accounts for 2025 say it has bought units in an investment fund called BISIP K, managed by the Bank for International Settlements, worth 205,811 million FCFA on 31 December 2025, down from 222,297 million FCFA a year earlier, and that it has joined the RAMP fund, the Reserve Advisory Management Program managed by the World Bank, worth 138,800 million FCFA on 31 December 2025, down from 149,873 million FCFA a year earlier. Together the two sets of fund units came to 344,611 million FCFA at the end of 2025, and the accounts group the BISIP K units with the holdings kept for immediate liquidity.

2011-01-22 · forced resignation. The Central Bank of West African States is the central bank of eight countries, and in January 2011 its own member heads of state removed its governor. After the disputed Ivorian presidential election of November 2010, the bank recognised Alassane Ouattara as head of state and revoked Laurent Gbagbo's access to Ivorian state accounts in December, and the union's finance ministers decided on 23 December that only representatives of Ouattara's government would have signing authority. The Ouattara camp complained in mid-January that the bank was still channelling cash to Gbagbo, and the governor, Philippe-Henry Dacoury-Tabley, an Ivorian and a close confidant of Gbagbo, was accused of not cooperating. At an emergency summit of the heads of state of the West African Economic and Monetary Union in Bamako on 22 January 2011 he handed in his resignation. The bank's own statement, issued in Dakar that evening, said the resignation resulted from pressure from the region's leaders. He told reporters afterwards: "I agreed to hand in my resignation as that is what was asked of me", and defended his conduct by pointing to practical and technical reasons for not transferring control of the accounts. The union accepted the resignation and called on Ouattara to propose a successor; a deputy governor, Jean-Baptiste Compaore, took over in the interim. Gbagbo's administration, on state television it still controlled, rejected what it called the forced resignation of the governor and rejected the leaders' decision to let Ouattara name a replacement. The European Union listed Dacoury-Tabley, giving as its ground that as governor of the BCEAO he refused to recognise the authority of the democratically elected President and was helping to fund the illegitimate administration of Mr Laurent Gbagbo. West African CFA franc (WAEMU/UMOA) – France cooperation (external guarantee)

The currency (XOF) is fixed at EUR 1 = 655.957 CFA francs.
France gives an unconditional and unlimited convertibility guarantee through advances to the central bank if its foreign exchange reserves run out.
A new cooperation agreement was signed in Abidjan on 21 December 2019, replacing the 1973 agreement; France stated the reform would enter into force in 2020.
The 2019 agreement ended the centralisation of BCEAO reserves at the French Treasury, ending the requirement that the BCEAO hold at least 50% of its reserves there.
The BCEAO's operations account at the French Treasury was closed in April 2021 (French Senate report); the Treasury page states it has had no operations account since January 2020.
France approved the agreement by Law no. 2021-108 of 3 February 2021.

CENTRAL BANK OF WEST AFRICAN STATES (BCEAO)
Burkina Faso
Burkina Faso uses the West African CFA franc, issued by the Central Bank of West African States, the BCEAO, which sets monetary policy for eight member countries. The franc is pegged, meaning held at a fixed rate, at one euro to 655.957 CFA francs, and France promises to advance euros if the bank's reserves run out; an agreement signed on 21 December 2019 ended the requirement that at least half those reserves sit at the French Treasury. One case is recorded: a summit of UEMOA heads of state accepted governor Dacoury-Tabley's resignation in January 2011, after he was criticized for ignoring a 23 December decision by UEMOA finance ministers that gave Alassane Ouattara power over the institution, and the article says the BCEAO paid out 60 to 100 billion CFA francs to the Gbagbo regime afterwards. The bank's own statement said the resignation resulted from pressure from the region's leaders, and Dacoury-Tabley said afterwards that he agreed to hand it in because that is what was asked of him. Abdoulaye Wade asked for an audit and alleged the former governor moved 500 billion CFA francs to Gbagbo; that is unproven. Its money is printed in France. The French foreign ministry's own page on the Franc Zone says the African central banks place the orders for notes and coins under a contract with a manufacturer, in this case the Banque de France, and that CFA franc notes and coins have been made at its works at Chamalieres since 1945; the heads of state and government of the Franc Zone may decide together to change where they are printed. The Banque de France's own director general of banknote manufacturing has called the BCEAO its largest export customer. The BCEAO's published accounts do not name the maker. Its gold is mostly not in Africa. Note 6 of the BCEAO's own financial statements for 2024 lists three places: the bank's head office, the Banque de France and the Bank for International Settlements. On deposit at the Banque de France are 1,054,479.65 ounces, valued at 1,756,111 million CFA francs, out of a stock of about 1.52 million ounces worth 2,531,800 million, which is about 70 per cent; press reporting places it in the Banque de France's underground vault in the first arrondissement of Paris. The Bank for International Settlements holds close to 106,000 ounces, and only about 120,000 ounces, under 8 per cent, sit physically at the head office in Dakar. In the 2018 statements the Paris deposit was 85 per cent of holdings; the share has fallen because the rest of the stock grew, not because gold left Paris. Answering Senator Pierre Laurent on 20 October 2022, the French economy ministry said the rules for the deposit are set by a specific convention covering the services the Banque de France provides to the BCEAO, and that the gold, like the union's foreign exchange reserves, is pooled at the BCEAO rather than apportioned by country. The concentration is contested: pan-Africanist currents and some economists read it as a continuing post-colonial dependence and ask whether the gold will be repatriated as the member states' operating account deposits at the French Treasury were. Part of the reserves is run by outside institutions. The BCEAO's own audited accounts for 2025 say it has bought units in an investment fund called BISIP K, managed by the Bank for International Settlements, worth 205,811 million FCFA on 31 December 2025, down from 222,297 million FCFA a year earlier, and that it has joined the RAMP fund, the Reserve Advisory Management Program managed by the World Bank, worth 138,800 million FCFA on 31 December 2025, down from 149,873 million FCFA a year earlier. Together the two sets of fund units came to 344,611 million FCFA at the end of 2025, and the accounts group the BISIP K units with the holdings kept for immediate liquidity. The accounts are audited by firms appointed in pairs, one doing the work and one standing in: Groupement PKF BAGE SARL et CROWE TG ICAAF with Deloitte Cote d'Ivoire for Burkina Faso, and Deloitte Cote d'Ivoire with Mazars Senegal for the BCEAO itself.

BANGLADESH BANK
Bangladesh
Bangladesh Bank issues the taka, printed at Gazipur by the Security Printing Corporation (Bangladesh) Ltd, known locally as Takshal. On the night of 4 February 2016 attackers used the bank's access to SWIFT, the network banks use to send payment instructions, to take reserves from its account at the New York Federal Reserve: 101 million dollars by The Daily Star's figure, 81 million extracted by Prothom Alo's. A government inquiry's final report of 30 May 2016 hinted that central bank officials were involved, but it was never published and no one had been punished as of 2019. Governor Atiur Rahman resigned on 15 March 2016, having been criticised for not telling Finance Minister Abul Maal Abdul Muhith, who called the bank's handling very incompetent. The Anti-Corruption Commission prosecuted Atiur in February 2025 over the AnonTex loan scam and in June 2025 opened an investigation into him over alleged abuse of power and the Hallmark and S Alam Group frauds; former deputy governor SK Sur was arrested on 14 January 2025 for failing to submit an asset statement, after a 2022 investigation into allegations he helped and gained from PK Halder's loan scam. Neither is proven. Governor Abdur Rouf Talukder resigned on 9 August 2024 citing health, three days after more than a hundred of the bank's own staff stormed his office demanding he go. Its gold is stored abroad rather than managed for it: the Bank of England holds about 188,927 troy ounces, used in lending, Standard Chartered 92,739 ounces and HSBC 93,535. Bangladesh scores 41 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed. Bangladesh Bank's own accounts are audited by two Dhaka firms together, Howladar Yunus & Co. and ACNABIN, whose joint report for 2024-2025 was signed on 26 August 2025 and is addressed to the Government rather than to the bank's board.

BULGARIAN NATIONAL BANK
Bulgaria
Bulgaria's central bank is the Bulgarian National Bank. On 1 January 2026 the country swapped the lev for the euro at 1.95583 lev to the euro and joined the Eurosystem, the group of national central banks that works with the European Central Bank, so its governor now sits on the body that sets interest rates. Its own large case concerns Corporate Commercial Bank, Corpbank, which collapsed in June 2014: prosecutors charged two former deputy governors responsible for supervision with failing, from February 2010, to take the measures the law required against the bank, allegedly to benefit its shareholders. Gounev was charged in June 2014 and removed from office by court order that December, and Simeonov about ten months later; neither charge is proven, and the accusation that Corpbank's majority owner embezzled 206 million leva is likewise unproven. The state's Bulgarian National Audit Office checks the books under a continuing legal mandate, Oberthur Fiduciaire AD has handled banknote production since 2014, and Louisenthal supplied the thread, foil and watermark for the 100-lev note that became legal tender on 28 December 2018. The bank is one of the 63 central banks that own the Bank for International Settlements, and belongs to the World Bank Treasury's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership, which offers advice, training or asset management without the page saying which Bulgaria uses. About 60 per cent of its 41 tonnes of gold sits outside its own vaults, stored at the Bank of England, which stores the metal rather than managing it. Two findings sit at the European Central Bank: the European Ombudsman found maladministration over President Mario Draghi's membership of the Group of Thirty, a forum whose members include private bankers, and recommended in January 2018 that he suspend it, which the ECB declined; and a speech by Coeure to a private London event on 18 May 2015 about front-loading asset purchases was published only the following morning, which the ECB called an internal procedure error. Kalin Hristov, long a member of the Governing Council and deputy governor for the Issue Department, joined the supervisory board of the commercial DSK Bank in August 2025; no ethics finding is recorded. Bulgaria scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.

CENTRAL BANK OF BAHRAIN
Bahrain
The Central Bank of Bahrain, created in 1973, issues the Bahraini Dinar (BHD), held at a peg to the US dollar as of December 2025. Its exposure score is 28 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed. The weakest side is corruption and secrecy around it (56): the country's laws hide who owns money, and financial secrecy scores 69 of 100. Written independence from government scores 0.515 of 1 on one index (rank 135 of 155) and 0.433 on another (rank 156 of 191). Government pressure was reported in 0 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018, and no documented case at the bank was found. A swap line, which is an agreement to borrow another central bank's currency, runs both ways with the United Arab Emirates: BHD 2 billion (AED 20 billion), signed 8 April 2026, for up to 5 years. De La Rue printed the 20-dinar note. The bank's accounts are audited by KPMG Fakhro of Manama, which signed its report on the 2023 financial statements on 10 March 2024. Rasheed Mohammed Al Maraj has been Governor since January 2005; immediately before joining the bank he was General Manager and Chief Executive Officer of the Arab Petroleum Investments Company, APICORP, in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, and earlier he was Assistant Under-Secretary at Bahrain's Ministry of Finance and National Economy and Under-Secretary at the Ministry of Transportation.

Bahamas
The Central Bank of The Bahamas issues the Bahamian dollar, which as of December 2025 is held at a fixed rate against the United States dollar. James H. The Independent Auditors' Report in the bank's 2011 annual report carries two signature blocks, Deloitte & Touche and BDO, each signed as Chartered Accountants at Nassau on 16 April 2012; later reports print that page as a scanned image.

James H. Smith, CBE (Governor of the Central Bank of The Bahamas, 1987-1997; Chairman of CFAL, no dates given): central bank governor to Chairman of CFAL, an investment management and brokerage firm. CFAL, a Nassau financial firm, says on its own leadership page that James H. Smith is its Chairman and that he was Governor of the Central Bank of The Bahamas from 1987 to 1997. The page also lists public roles: Senator and Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance from 2002 to 2007, Undersecretary in the Cabinet Office, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Finance, Ambassador for Trade, and chairmanships of the Bahamas Maritime Authority, the Paradise Island Bridge Company and the Bahamas Development Bank, which is a government development bank. It says he has been a director on several private sector boards, without naming them, and gives no dates for the CFAL chairmanship. CFAL's own 'about' page describes the firm as 'a leading independent investment management and advisory firm based in Nassau, Bahamas', offering pension administration, brokerage and private wealth services, and says CFAL is 'the investment arm of Colina Holdings Ltd'. Neither page uses the words privately owned or government-owned, so the firm's ownership is stated only through that parent-company description. The private side of this career is CFAL; the Bahamas Development Bank and the ministry posts are the public side. James Smith - Leadership (CFAL)
T. Baswell Donaldson, CBE (first Governor and Board Chairman of the Central Bank of The Bahamas, 1 June 1974 to May 1980): from Governor of the Central Bank of The Bahamas to chairman of the commercial bank Commonwealth Bank; ownership not stated. The Central Bank of The Bahamas' own former-governors page states that T. Baswell Donaldson was appointed the first Governor and Board Chairman of the Central Bank on 1 June 1974 and served until May 1980. Before that he was Manager of The Bahamas Monetary Authority from 1968 to 1972 and its Chairman from 1972 to 1974, and he began his career as Assistant Secretary in the Ministry of Finance and later served as Controller of Exchange. The same page states that after leaving the Central Bank he chaired Commonwealth Bank, a Bahamian commercial bank, as well as the Securities Commission and the College of The Bahamas Council, and served as Ambassador to the United States. The central bank's page gives no dates for the Commonwealth Bank chairmanship beyond placing it after he demitted office in May 1980, and it does not say whether Commonwealth Bank is privately owned or state-owned. The Securities Commission and the College Council are public bodies. This is a different person from James H. Smith, whose record The Bahamas already holds. The convertible mark is issued by the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina under a currency board: marks are put into circulation only against convertible foreign currency the bank holds, at 1.95583 marks to the euro, and its monetary liabilities may never exceed its foreign currency assets. The National Bank of the Republic of Belarus issues the Belarusian ruble and holds it within 2 percent of a mix of the euro, the Russian ruble and the US dollar. On 18 July 2011 the state news agency Belta reported that President Alyaksandr Lukashenka had relieved Pyotr Prokopovich of his duties as chief of the National Bank of Belarus by decree, with no official reason given; Prokopovich had led the bank since 1998, had heart surgery in April 2011 and had been replaced on an acting basis in June by Yury Alymov while he recovered, and the dismissal came during an economic crisis marked by rising inflation, a sharp currency devaluation and government price controls on some key goods. Kasperovich admitted the charges in full; the rest remains unproven. Belarus also has two agreements with China, from 2010 and 2015, to borrow its currency. CENTRAL BANK OF BRAZIL
Brazil
Brazil's money is the real, issued by the Central Bank of Brazil. On 3 October 2019 the Federal Police and federal prosecutors in Sao Paulo opened Operation Estrela Cadente into leaks of the bank's interest-rate decisions in 2010, 2011 and 2012, said to have benefited a fund of the bank BTG Pactual; the investigation covered corruption, inside information and money laundering and is still open, so nothing is proven. On 21 June 2024 President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva called the bank's president, Roberto Campos Neto, his political and ideological adversary and said Brazil would return to normality once he could replace him. Three leaders crossed between the bank and private finance: Meirelles, president from 2003 to 2010, held posts at BankBoston, FleetBoston and Lazard Americas; Ilan Goldfajn, governor from May 2016 to February 2019, at Banco Itau Unibanco and Credit Suisse Brazil; and Campos Neto came from Santander and was to join Nubank as vice chairman on 1 July 2025, after a legally required six-month wait. Its notes come from Casa da Moeda, contracted on 13 April 2017 for 980 million notes worth 279.14 million reais. Brazil scores 27 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.

p:BRB:
CENTRAL BANK OF BARBADOS
Barbados
The Central Bank of Barbados issues the Barbados dollar and in practice holds it at a fixed rate against the United States dollar. In 2017 Finance Minister Chris Sinckler dismissed Governor Delisle Worrell. The government's stated reason was that the board objected to his reported high-handed manner; some observers believed the reason was his refusal to keep financing the government with new money, which he had set out in a letter that January saying the government must stop taking new money from the bank to pay its bills. The Appeals Court upheld the minister's right to dismiss him. Apart from that, no government pressure was reported in the 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018. The bank's founding governor, Sir Courtney Blackman, had been an economist at the Wall Street bank Irving Trust Company from 1968 to 1971, led the bank from 1972 to 1987 across three terms while also serving as Barbados' alternate governor to the International Monetary Fund until March 1987, and from 1987 to 1994 worked as an international business consultant and as director general of corporations and financial institutions that the bank's own page does not name. Its five-dollar polymer note, introduced in December 2022, is printed by De La Rue. Barbados scores 28 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and the bank tells the public little, 3 of 15 on a transparency measure. The bank's accounts are audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers SRL of Bridgetown, whose report for the year ended 31 December 2025 is dated 27 March 2026.

BRUNEI DARUSSALAM CENTRAL BANK
Brunei
Brunei Darussalam Central Bank issues the Brunei dollar and runs it as a currency board, meaning the dollar is held at a fixed rate against the Singapore dollar. Under an agreement set up in 1967, the Brunei bank and Singapore's monetary authority each take in the other's notes and coins from banks and exchange them at par without charge. Note Printing Australia has printed notes for Brunei: the Reserve Bank of Australia's 2007 report lists the Brunei Currency and Monetary Board among that printer's export orders in 2006/07, without giving a number of notes. PricewaterhouseCoopers Services audits the accounts. No case at the bank is documented. ROYAL MONETARY AUTHORITY OF BHUTAN
Bhutan
Bhutan's central bank is the Royal Monetary Authority, which issues the ngultrum and keeps it pegged, or fixed, to the Indian rupee; the rupee circulates in the country as well. An anonymous informer raised a case in October 2014, and the final findings of Bhutan's Anti-Corruption Commission, covering 2014 to 2016, said a former deputy governor had allegedly forged official documents, misused power and concealed earnings from World Bank and Asian Development Bank projects. Those allegations are unproven; the case was forwarded to the Office of the Attorney General, with no later outcome. A currency swap with India, letting each side borrow up to 100 million US dollars, was signed on 17 March 2016 and ran out in March 2019. A commemorative 1,000-ngultrum note marking the Fourth King's seventieth birth anniversary was printed by De La Rue, not the ordinary circulating series, and the accounts for 2003 and 2004 were audited by M/s P.K. BANK OF BOTSWANA
Botswana
The Bank of Botswana issues the pula, which it manages against the South African rand, moving the rate in small steps within a narrow band. One case is recorded and it ended in acquittal. A woman arrested on 17 October 2019 was accused, with others including former president Ian Khama and former intelligence head Isaac Kgosi, of stealing 100 billion pula from the bank. High Court judge Zein Kebonang discharged and acquitted her of unexplained property and a false passport declaration, the state withdrew a terrorism financing charge, and he found the accusations fabricated and referred the investigator to police for perjury prosecution. The accusations against the others remain unproven. One career move is documented: Linah Kelebogile Mohohlo joined the bank on 20 April 1976, worked at the International Monetary Fund from 1994 to 1996 under its Special Appointee Programme, in the African Department and the Monetary and Capital Markets Department, and later served as the bank's Governor and Chairman of the Board from 20 October 1999 until she retired in October 2016, having earlier been Deputy Governor and the founding director of its foreign department. Northern Trust works for the bank on measuring and explaining how its investments have performed and on training staff, which the source describes as reporting and training rather than management of its assets. The 10 pula polymer note that entered circulation on 1 February 2018 was designed and printed by De La Rue. EY audits the accounts. Botswana scores 23 of 100 on exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed.

p:CAF:
BANK OF CENTRAL AFRICAN STATES (BEAC)
Central African Republic
The Central African Republic uses the Central African CFA franc (XAF), issued by the Bank of Central African States (BEAC), which sets monetary policy for 6 members. The franc is fixed at EUR 1 = 655.957 CFA francs. France guarantees convertibility without limit, and the BEAC must deposit at least 50% of its foreign exchange reserves at the French Treasury (lowered from 65% in 2007). Exposure score is 47 of 100, where 0 means shielded from outside influence and 100 means fully exposed. The BEAC scores 0.5 of 15 on transparency, last of 112, and government pressure to cut rates or ease was reported in 3 of 37 quarters from 2010 to 2018. One case: a November 2009 internal report found about 20 billion CFA francs diverted from the Paris office to 139 beneficiaries between 2004 and 2008. On 28 September 2012 a court in Mfoundi, Cameroon, sentenced Kemadjou to life imprisonment and ordered him to pay BEAC 26.4 billion CFA francs. Philibert Andzembe, a Gabonese national, had been governor of the bank since July 2007, and in October 2009 Gabon's president Ali Bongo fired him in response to a scandal in which 28.3 million US dollars went missing from the bank's Paris branch; Gabon held the right to appoint the governor at the time, and Lucas Abaga Nchama of Equatorial Guinea took the post in 2010. A separate leaked US diplomatic cable, made public in December 2010, alleged that Gabonese officials working at the bank had taken about 36 million US dollars from the pooled reserves over roughly five years. The reserves the BEAC must keep at the French Treasury sit in an operations account (compte d'operations) opened in the BEAC's name. The required share earns interest at the European Central Bank's marginal lending facility rate, 0.25 per cent since 16 March 2016, and anything the BEAC chooses to deposit above that share earns the ECB's minimum rate on main refinancing operations, 0 per cent since 16 March 2016. KPMG Afrique Centrale and Mazars Cameroun audit the accounts jointly. Its money is printed in France. The French foreign ministry's own page on the Franc Zone says the African central banks place the orders for notes and coins under a contract with a manufacturer, in this case the Banque de France, and that CFA franc notes and coins have been made at its works at Chamalieres since 1945; the heads of state and government of the Franc Zone may decide together to change where they are printed. The BEAC's own site cannot be read by automated requests, so this does not rest on a BEAC document.

Central African CFA franc (CEMAC/UMAC) – France cooperation (external guarantee)

The currency (XAF) is fixed at EUR 1 = 655.957 CFA francs; the euro replaced the French franc as anchor on 1 January 1999 with no change in parity.
France provides an unlimited convertibility guarantee, committing euro funds if the sub-region cannot pay for imports in foreign currency.
The BEAC must deposit at least 50% of its foreign exchange reserves in its operations account at the French Treasury (lowered from 65% in 2007).
Mandatory deposits earn the ECB marginal lending facility rate (stated as 0.25% since 16 March 2016); amounts above earn the ECB main refinancing rate; holdings are protected against euro depreciation against the SDR.
France designates two BEAC administrators and two Monetary Policy Committee members, the same number as each of the six CEMAC states.
A France–CEMAC ministers and governors meeting on 17 March 2026 discussed reserves, public finances and integration; the French Treasury's account records no decision changing the operations account, reserve deposit, French representation or currency name. The next meeting in this format is planned for 2027.
The CFA franc was devalued 50% on 11 January 1994.

SWISS NATIONAL BANK
Switzerland
Switzerland's money is the Swiss franc, issued by the Swiss National Bank, a joint-stock company listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange with 100,000 shares and 25 million francs of capital. At the end of 2025 the 26 cantons held 38.995 per cent, 24 cantonal banks 11.966 per cent, 19 municipalities 0.265 per cent and private shareholders 48.774 per cent; the largest single holders were the Canton of Berne with 6.63 per cent, the Canton of Zurich with 5.23 per cent and one private holder, Theo Siegert, with 5.01 per cent. Holders outside the public sector may vote no more than 100 shares each, and the Confederation owns none. Orell Fussli Security Printing prints the notes, KPMG has audited the accounts since 2015, and the bank part-owns the Bank for International Settlements. About 70 per cent of its gold is stored in Switzerland, some 20 per cent at the Bank of England and roughly 10 per cent at the Bank of Canada; those two store the gold and do not manage its money. It scores 32 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. One case and one episode of pressure are recorded, and both are the same affair. Chairman Philipp Hildebrand resigned on 9 January 2012, with immediate effect, less than two years into the job. His wife Kashya, a former currency trader, had bought 504,000 dollars in August 2011 and sold the position three weeks later for a profit of 75,000 francs, after the bank had intervened to weaken the franc. Details of the family's private bank transactions were leaked by an IT worker at Bank Sarasin to a lawyer sitting in the Thurgau cantonal parliament for the Swiss People's Party, and Switzerland's highest court later imposed suspended fines on both men. Christoph Blocher, the party's leading figure, had long called for Hildebrand to go and passed documents on the trades to the government; the party weekly Weltwoche said it had proof the trades were Hildebrand's own. The party was at the time campaigning against the bank's policy of buying euros to hold the franc at 1.20. Hildebrand denied wrongdoing on 5 January and refused to resign; four days later he resigned, saying he could not prove beyond doubt that he had been unaware of his wife's transactions, and he gave the profits to charity. A later inquiry cleared him of insider trading, a criminal investigation was dropped, and the bank tightened its rules on staff financial dealings. He joined BlackRock as vice chairman in 2012. Jean-Pierre Roth, chairman of the Governing Board from 2001 to 2009, was elected to the board of the reinsurer Swiss Re in 2010. Neither move carries an ethics finding.

CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE
Chile
Chile's central bank is the Central Bank of Chile, which issues the Chilean peso. It scores 24 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence, and no government pressure was reported between 2010 and 2018. The Constitutional Convention elected to write a replacement for the 1980 constitution drafted new articles on the bank, and on 5 April 2022 its president Rosanna Costa wrote to the Convention on the Council's behalf setting out what it objected to. The main objection was the removal provision: one third of the members of Congress could have asked the Supreme Court to remove councillors, which the bank said exposed it to political judgements that would diminish its autonomy and its working. It asked that the power to request removal be limited to a majority of the councillors or to the President of the Republic, and that the organic law's standard be written in, so that the conduct must have been the main and direct cause of significant damage to the country's economy. It also asked that productive diversification be struck from the list of its objectives, as not a monetary task. Voters rejected the draft on 4 September 2022. Two cases are recorded, both still under investigation. On 24 July 2012 three staff allegedly tried to take about 38 million pesos in banknotes being processed for destruction, and a fourth was detained the next day; the bank told the police economic crimes unit and began legal action. In March 2022 someone posing as the finance chief of the US firm RVK sent a false invoice for 205,000 dollars from an address one letter off the real one, and the bank paid. It complained to prosecutors in May 2022, said no official appeared to have taken part deliberately, and dismissed its accounting management head that June; he sued in December, seeking 267 million pesos. Part of the state's sovereign wealth funds is run by outside firms the bank picks and supervises, BlackRock holding the high yield and corporate bond portfolios and Nomura Asset Management part of the high yield bonds. KPMG audits the accounts.

2022-04-05 · attempted law change. Chile's Constitutional Convention, elected to write a replacement for the 1980 constitution, drafted new articles on the Banco Central de Chile in its Commission 6 on justice systems, autonomous oversight bodies and constitutional reform. On 5 April 2022 the bank's president Rosanna Costa wrote to the president of the Convention on behalf of the bank's Council, in official letter 114, setting out what the Council objected to. Its main objection was to the removal provision: the draft allowed one third of the members of Congress to ask the Supreme Court to remove councillors, which the bank said exposed the institution to a complex situation and to political judgements that would diminish its autonomy and its working. The Council asked that the power to request removal be limited to a majority of the councillors or to the President of the Republic, and that the existing organic law's standard be written in, so that a removed councillor's conduct must have been the main and direct cause of significant damage to the country's economy. It also asked that productive diversification be struck from the list of the bank's objectives, on the ground that it is not a monetary task, and that the rule in the current constitution's article 109 barring the bank from discriminating between parties be restored, as the draft had dropped it. On the governance articles the letter said changes should not diminish the effectiveness of the institution's autonomy, and it noted that appointment by the President of the Republic had not harmed the bank's autonomy. When the plenary voted on 4 May 2022 it approved the bank's existence and its autonomy but sent the articles on its powers, limits and the appointment of councillors back to committee for lack of the 103 votes needed. Voters rejected the draft constitution on 4 September 2022, so none of it took effect. Oficio ORD. PEOPLE'S BANK OF CHINA
China
China's money, the renminbi, is issued by the People's Bank of China. The country scores 35 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, and the weakest part is corruption and secrecy around the bank. Written independence scores 0.659 of 1 on an index of 42 legal rules, but the part covering the governor and the board scores only 0.04, meaning the government holds nearly all of that power; pressure from government was reported in 2 of 37 quarters surveyed between 2010 and 2018. One case is documented: in October 2024 the Huanggang Intermediate People's Court sentenced Fan Yifei, a former deputy governor, to death with a two-year reprieve, to be commuted to life without parole, for accepting property worth more than 386 million yuan through his posts at the central bank and other institutions including China Construction Bank. A year before that sentence, in September 2023, the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection, the Communist Party's own disciplinary body, announced that Fan Yifei had been expelled from the party and dismissed from public office for serious violation of discipline and law. The commission alleged that he accepted banquets, travel, golf and private club access against the rules, took gifts and cash, had relatives paid without working, traded his position for personal gain and sex, interfered in law enforcement, used his financial role to obtain loans for others and illegally accepted large amounts of property, and it said his illegal gains would be confiscated and that he would be prosecuted in accordance with the law; these were the commission's own findings and allegations, which had not at that point been tested in court. Its notes and coins are made by the China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation, described as a state company inside the bank, though only Wikipedia was found saying so, and the National Audit Office audits the accounts. One career move is documented: Zhou Xiaochuan spent two years as president of China Construction Bank, a large state commercial bank, then was chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, the state securities regulator, from 2000 to 2002, and then became governor of the People's Bank of China; no years are given for the China Construction Bank post. The governor, Pan Gongsheng, two former governors and a monetary policy committee member sit in the Group of Thirty, a private forum alongside the chief executive of Citi and a vice chairman of BlackRock. Its reach is wide: 89 swap lines, which are standing agreements to lend its currency to another central bank, 8.6 percent of world currency trading and 2,346.4 tonnes of gold.

p:CIV:
CENTRAL BANK OF WEST AFRICAN STATES (BCEAO)
Côte d'Ivoire
Côte d'Ivoire uses the West African CFA franc, issued by the Central Bank of West African States, the BCEAO, which sets monetary policy for eight member countries. The franc is pegged — held at a fixed rate — at 655.957 to the euro, and France promises to advance euros if the bank's reserves run out; a 2019 agreement ended the rule that it keep at least half its reserves at the French Treasury. The country scores 43 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed. Two cases come out of the post-election crisis of December 2010 to April 2011. On 18 January 2018 a court sentenced Laurent Gbagbo, Aké N'Gbo, Katinan and Dallo to 20 years and a fine of 329 billion CFA francs for offences including group theft by break-in of BCEAO vaults and cash; seven bailiffs got 36 months and a 700,000 CFA franc fine, Katinan was absent throughout, Gbagbo always denied the charges, and on 6 August 2022 President Ouattara pardoned him. Earlier, in January 2011, a summit of UEMOA heads of state accepted governor Dacoury-Tabley's resignation, after he was criticized for ignoring a 23 December decision by UEMOA finance ministers that gave Alassane Ouattara power over the institution; the account says the bank paid 60 to 100 billion CFA francs to the Gbagbo regime after that date, and Senegal's President Abdoulaye Wade asked for an audit and alleged 500 billion CFA francs had been moved, with no audit result given. The bank's own statement said the resignation resulted from pressure from the region's leaders, and Dacoury-Tabley said afterwards that he agreed to hand it in because that is what was asked of him. Days later Gbagbo ordered the seizure of the bank's Ivorian branches, after it said it would no longer honour his signature; Ouattara ordered those branches closed and said anyone following Gbagbo's orders would be prosecuted. His prime minister, Guillaume Soro, said that when Gbagbo goes to the BCEAO in Abidjan with tanks and Kalashnikovs he cannot but trigger bank closures and halt cash flow. On 9 February 2011 the Gbagbo administration also seized the regional stock exchange, the Bourse Regionale des Valeurs Mobilieres, which then stopped operating in Abidjan, and international banks left the country. Its money is printed in France. The French foreign ministry's own page on the Franc Zone says the African central banks place the orders for notes and coins under a contract with a manufacturer, in this case the Banque de France, and that CFA franc notes and coins have been made at its works at Chamalieres since 1945; the heads of state and government of the Franc Zone may decide together to change where they are printed. The Banque de France's own director general of banknote manufacturing has called the BCEAO its largest export customer. The BCEAO's published accounts do not name the maker. Its gold is mostly not in Africa. Note 6 of the BCEAO's own financial statements for 2024 lists three places: the bank's head office, the Banque de France and the Bank for International Settlements. On deposit at the Banque de France are 1,054,479.65 ounces, valued at 1,756,111 million CFA francs, out of a stock of about 1.52 million ounces worth 2,531,800 million, which is about 70 per cent; press reporting places it in the Banque de France's underground vault in the first arrondissement of Paris. The Bank for International Settlements holds close to 106,000 ounces, and only about 120,000 ounces, under 8 per cent, sit physically at the head office in Dakar. In the 2018 statements the Paris deposit was 85 per cent of holdings; the share has fallen because the rest of the stock grew, not because gold left Paris. Answering Senator Pierre Laurent on 20 October 2022, the French economy ministry said the rules for the deposit are set by a specific convention covering the services the Banque de France provides to the BCEAO, and that the gold, like the union's foreign exchange reserves, is pooled at the BCEAO rather than apportioned by country. The concentration is contested: pan-Africanist currents and some economists read it as a continuing post-colonial dependence and ask whether the gold will be repatriated as the member states' operating account deposits at the French Treasury were. Part of the reserves is run by outside institutions. The BCEAO's own audited accounts for 2025 say it has bought units in an investment fund called BISIP K, managed by the Bank for International Settlements, worth 205,811 million FCFA on 31 December 2025, down from 222,297 million FCFA a year earlier, and that it has joined the RAMP fund, the Reserve Advisory Management Program managed by the World Bank, worth 138,800 million FCFA on 31 December 2025, down from 149,873 million FCFA a year earlier. Together the two sets of fund units came to 344,611 million FCFA at the end of 2025, and the accounts group the BISIP K units with the holdings kept for immediate liquidity.
